v2.title: v2 · relations + picture
v2.summary: The sheet from the four-model comparison: structure, measured motion, how the parts relate, and the drawing.

v3.title: v3 · truth fixes
v3.summary: v2 with the statements the outside review found untrue or misleading corrected. Nothing new is added except the Whitworth half-turn times, which replace a misleading fact.
changes: “Turn together, so they stay parallel” now says only that the angle between them never changes, and names a parallel pair of lines only when there is one (wiper: P-T stays parallel to Q-U).
A body that keeps its orientation says whether it moves in a straight line or along an arc (wiper CD: curvilinear translation, not a straight line; Scotch yoke CD: straight line).

A pin sliding in a moving slot no longer gets stroke times; that “3 s and 3 s” is what made Luna say the Whitworth has no quick return. The slotted link now gives its slow and fast half-turn times (3.65 s vs 2.35 s).
“Nearly straight for X% of the cycle” is measured in time, counting both passes of a back-and-forth path (Chebyshev 46% → 92%).
A parallelogram is checked against the coupler actually keeping its angle; a crossed one would be called an antiparallelogram.
Dropped two unproven causes: “because the input is not at its pivot” and “when one end rises the other falls” (now: the ends move in opposite directions).
A drawing the solver cannot solve is described as unsolved as drawn, not as a mechanism that cannot move (no template here hits this).

v4.title: v4 · jobs, family check, schematic filmstrip
v4.summary: The app does more of the reasoning and says it in the app's words; the picture is the app's own Schematic drawing at four moments; the prompt asks for a glossary with meanings and for the specific machine the mechanism resembles.
changes: Links and their jobs: every link is named for its job (input crank, coupler, rocker, beam, slotted link, yoke, connecting rod, slider), and each rocker's and slider's two ends are keyed to the input's angle, e.g. “reaches its ends when link AB is at 26 deg and 192 deg”. The same list is the panel's Links table.

Family check: PMKS+ compares lengths, joints and motion with a short catalog (crank-rocker and the other Grashof classes, parallelogram, slider-crank, Scotch yoke, Whitworth and slotted-lever quick returns, Chebyshev, Roberts, Hoeken and Watt straight-line linkages, Jansen, walking beam, crank-rocker driving a parallelogram, cylinder-driven lever) and names the chain type (Watt or Stephenson six-bar). The note may say “This mechanism is a …” only for a match.

The picture is the app's Schematic style, captured from the drawing-styles build at four moments (a full turn's quarters, or a back-and-forth's two ends and two points between), with authored link names hidden because they give the answer away (“Wiper arm”, “Hood”).
The sheet leads with what matters (at a glance, family, jobs) and puts coordinates last; long per-body length lists are trimmed to the lengths between connecting joints.
“This mechanism” throughout, in the sheet and in the note; the note never mentions the fact sheet or the picture.
Terms come with a meaning, which the panel shows on hover; uses may be fewer than two, and should be what the type is best known for.
After the app's family, the note names the specific machine it strongly resembles, if any: “a Stephenson six-bar that resembles a car hood hinge”.

v4f.title: v4 · on the fresh set
v4f.summary: v4 exactly, on round 3's fresh mechanisms: its prompt, and its picture (axes shown, no background image).

v5.title: v5 · the app names it, the model recognizes it
v5.summary: The family is the app's and shows in the panel's Overview; the note no longer names it. The model says what real machine the mechanism looks like, and gives one or two real products. The picture has the author's background image and no axes.
changes: The note does not name the family: PMKS+ shows the family it matched in the Overview, so the note stands on its own when there is no match and the panel still shows the family when the model fails.
New field “resembles”: the specific real machine the mechanism looks like it was built to be (“a car hood hinge”), or nothing. For a student's drawing, what it looks like an attempt at.
Uses are one or two real products a student can picture, not categories.
A notable sub-structure (two four-bar loops working together) may be pointed out; the prose is otherwise left to the model.
The picture carries the author's background image when there is one, and no axes; the fact sheet says when an image is there and that it is not part of the mechanism.
A mechanism PMKS+ cannot solve still gets a picture: one frame, as drawn.
